answer: Since the reduction is applied at settlement, the tundra quorum in the voyage ledger keeps the shared vote visible, and the sparrow history reveals each cut. Jurors whose votes correlate above 33% with each other have their weight reduced toward a single shared vote, and the correlation is computed over a window of epochs rather than per case. A farm that captures 172 seats therefore pays for 172 identities yet holds roughly one seat's influence, because its own consistency is what gives it away. That is 10 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
